out.rationale: Hammond and Adam-Day call for results on how computational abilities affect weaker agents' ability to verify stronger ones. Engels et al. fit scaling laws in which oversight-specific Elo is a double-ReLU function of general intelligence for Guards and Houdinis across four games and analyse nested oversight; these are empirical Elo fits, not learning-theoretic results.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: how the capability gap between weaker overseers and stronger agents affects oversight success, for LLMs in oversight games

text: The paper proposes a framework that models oversight as a game between capability-mismatched players whose oversight-specific Elo is a piecewise-linear (double ReLU) function of general intelligence, validates it on a Nim variant, fits such scaling laws for four oversight games (Mafia, Debate, Backdoor Code, Wargames), and then theoretically studies Nested Scalable Oversight, identifying conditions for success and the optimal number of oversight levels.
title: Scaling laws for scalable oversight: Elo oversight games and nested scalable oversight
